headline_marked: Bluesky adds [[algorithmic opt-out]] for posts, preventing viral spread
headline: Bluesky adds algorithmic opt-out for posts, preventing viral spread
summary: Users can now choose to keep their posts within their personal network, opting out of the main Discover feed to avoid unwanted virality.
details: Bluesky has introduced a new feature allowing users to disable their posts from appearing in the app's main Discover feed. This move aims to give users more control over their content's reach, catering to those who prefer to post for their followers without seeking wider exposure.

The algorithmic feed currently surfaces any public post on the network. This new opt-out feature does not make posts private, as Bluesky is still developing protocol-level support for private data. Instead, it limits the discoverability of public posts to users outside of one's immediate network.

To activate this feature, users can navigate to the Privacy and Security settings within the Bluesky app and toggle the new option. The company notes that the change may take up to an hour to fully propagate across the platform.

Significantly, this preference is recorded at the account level, meaning it travels with the user across different applications built on the same AT Proto protocol. However, other apps using the protocol must choose to honor this setting for it to be effective beyond Bluesky itself.

headline_marked: Google Gemini Notebook [[interacts with books]] using AI
headline: Google Gemini Notebook interacts with books using AI
summary: The AI note-taking app now pulls information from your purchased Google Play Books, allowing you to ask questions and generate content based on their contents.
details: Google's Gemini Notebook has launched a new feature called 'Expert Intelligence' that allows users to interact with books they have purchased on Google Play Books. This AI-powered tool can answer questions about the book's content, generate plans, infographics, and even AI podcasts based on the material.

During a demonstration, the tool was used to generate a recipe book from Michael Pollan's 'Food Rules' and to answer a management question using Kim Scott's 'Radical Candor'. Users can also view the full text of the book directly within Notebook.

Initially, over 100,000 books from major publishers like Penguin Random House and Macmillan Publishers will support Expert Intelligence. Google has also collaborated with 15 authors to create 'Featured Notebooks' with additional source material and introductory content.

Google has implemented privacy protections to ensure that users cannot access content from books they have not purchased. If a Notebook containing a purchased book is shared, other users will see the book listed as a source but will not be able to view its full text or related information.

Google plans to integrate this feature into its AI Mode in Search and the Gemini app, which can already pull information from Gemini Notebook. Future expansions are planned to include scholarly articles, magazine articles, and newspapers.
